title: Annotatio VI §.I close: Reformed dispute Indigni Oral about absolute impious — stop before §.II
pass_a_gloss: But although the Reformed deny Oral Eating of Christ’s Body universally, by whomsoever, worthy or unworthy, it is said to be done; yet when they dispute with Lutherans about Oral Eating of Christ’s body by the Unworthy, they chiefly regard Unworthy of the former kind, pointing out that such Unworthy — i.e. habitually impious and unregenerate — in no way at all, and so neither by Oral Eating, become partakers of Christ’s body itself in the Holy Supper.
pass_b_english: The Reformed deny Oral eating of Christ’s body for anyone, worthy or unworthy.

Yet when they dispute Lutheran Oral-of-the-unworthy, they mainly mean the absolute kind — habitual impious and unregenerate — who in no way, Oral included, partake Christ’s body itself in the Supper. Stop §.I before §.II.
source_text: Etsi verò Reformati Oralem Corporis Christi Manducationem in universum inficiantur, à quocunque, digno, seu indigno, dicatur fieri; tamen quando de Indignorum corporis Christi Manducatione Orali, cum Lutheranis disputant, prioris generis Indignos potissimum respiciunt, indigitantes, hujusmodi Indignos, i. e. habitualiter impios ac irregeneratos, nullô planè modo, eóque nec Orali Manducatione, ipsius corporis Christi, in S. Cœna fieri participes.
